title: Sr. Analyst, Global Client Payments - Avalara
description:
Role Summary: 
 Global Client Payments reconciles and validates the payments Avalara makes on behalf of clients to tax authorities. Payment volume is growing across every line of business, and the team is investing in stronger reconciliation processes and AI-enabled workflows to support that growth. This role owns an established reconciliation process and the month-end close that runs alongside it. Daily reconciliations, exception resolution, and month-end close all run to fixed deadlines that partner teams and clients rely on. The role exists to raise the accuracy and timeliness of reconciliation and to convert manual reconciliation effort into repeatable, AI-supported process that makes the work faster and more reliable. 
 How This Role Elevates Avalara: 
 Reduces compliance risk by clearing exceptions and unpaid items within published turnaround targets Enhances client experience through accurate, timely reconciliation that reduces notices and penalties Improves month-end close reliability through complete, on-time delivery Prevents errors from reaching clients by catching breaks in peer reconciliations Improves decision quality by applying critical thinking across all reconciliation work Strengthens the control environment through current procedures and audit-ready evidence Increases operational scale by using AI to surface opportunities to improve reconciliation processes Raises team capability through documentation, process improvement, and AI best-practice sharing 
 Responsibilities: 
 Own daily reconciliations of bank activity against liability records, and clear exceptions within published turnaround targets Own month-end reconciliation close and deliver complete, accurate results on deadline Own creation and resolution of unpaid items, and keep aging within target Review reconciliations completed by other analysts, and catch errors before they impact clients Own presented-item and stop-payment decisions, exercising judgment within defined control requirements Own standard operating procedure (SOP) documentation, keeping it current and audit-ready Identify and implement process and AI-enabled improvements that reduce manual effort or improve accuracy Partner cross-functionally on unresolved items, and escalate with a recommendation, not just a problem Lead within the team by driving shared work to delivery and keeping peers unblocked Raise peer capability through onboarding support, knowledge sharing, and coaching. 
 AI Expectations: 
 This role is built for someone who uses AI to create real leverage in speed, accuracy, insight, and scale. 
 How you will show up in the role today 
 Spot opportunities to use AI to surface mismatches, aging patterns, and unpaid item trends faster, and work with the team to test and validate those approaches before they touch live work Build reusable prompts for recurring tasks like drafting exception narratives, summarizing unpaid item aging, and formatting variance explanations, and strengthen them through peer input before they become part of the teams toolkit Use AI to assist with SOP drafting, updates, and version comparisons, reducing the time it takes to keep documentation current after process changes Validate every AI-generated output against source data before it informs any reconciliation decision, presented-item judgment, or stop-payment action; AI assists; it does not decide 
 How this role will evolve as AI matures 
 As AI takes on more of the routine matching work, this role will shift toward owning the exception logic itself, defining the rules, thresholds, and escalation criteria that AI workflows operate within The analyst will increasingly serve as a quality control layer over AI outputs, spotting drift, validating edge cases, and flagging where AI confidence should not be trusted Process improvement will evolve from one-off efficiency gains to identifying where AI can be consistently embedded in recurring reconciliation tasks Documentation and knowledge transfer will carry more weight, as well-structured process knowledge enables more consistent execution across the team and makes AI assistance more accurate Candidates who can demonstrate this mindset, using AI confidently today while thinking clearly about where the role is heading, will stand out. 
 Bar Raiser

title: Product Design / Product Engineer/ Specialist
description:
Job Summary: This product focused position performs established technical tasks at the sub-system and/or component level for current and future products within a given business unit or corporate area. This involves work across many steps in the product life cycle. Because of the product centered nature of this position, they are very often a central point of coordination and decision making between product line engineers, customer teams, systems engineers, purchasing, suppliers and manufacturing. Key Responsibilities: Obtains input from stakeholders such as technical managers, project leaders, other product and manufacturing engineers and supplier partners to deliver information and recommendations that lead to quality product decisions. Applies academic knowledge and existing experience to take action and make decisions that progress projects forward without sacrificing project quality expectations. Examples of these decisions include day to day project details, analysis or test work instruction details, coordination across discipline areas that are necessary to make quality progress. Applies and improves processes such as Engineering Standard Work (ESW), iDFMEA, Failure Incident Review Group (FIRG) and tools such as 7-step problem solving, design review checklist and other specialized tools required to support the processes and enable high quality decision making. Provides independent leadership of smaller business impact projects or ownership of complex components, products, systems or services with greater elements of ambiguity over the senior or lead engineer level and with full accountability to the project team. Delivers independent execution of established and emerging work processes and systems, while still developing technology or product knowledge. Leads the development and improvement of work processes and systems across a functional discipline area within a business unit site. Coordinates and directs work amongst technicians and temporary student employees, assists in the transfer of knowledge to lesser experienced engineers through either indirect (scope of influence) or direct management of a small, local group of engineers. Provides support and guidance to influence technical direction within a project team and continues to develop proficiency in the competency areas critical to success in the role. Operates as a recognized specialist in a discipline or product area within the immediate team. Skills: Strong understanding of ADS components like Doser, Mixers and/or fuel systems components. Proficiency in 3D modeling tools (Creo) and engineering drawing standards (GD&T). Knowledge of design tools and methodologies (DFMEA, DFM, DFA, DV&V). Familiarity with Cummins processes (VPI, PPT, CPS) and tools (Windchill, RV&S). Ability to interpret simulation results (structural and flow analysis). Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Effective communication and collaboration abilities. Working knowledge of manufacturing processes and product validation techniques. Experience: 5+ years of experience in CES products or Fuel Systems product lines 6-8 years of product design and development experience preferred. Experience in cross-functional design reviews and product lifecycle processes. Familiarity with MS Office tools is preferred. Competencies: 
Product Development Execution, Monitoring and Control - Plans, schedules, coordinates and executes the activities involved in developing a product to a respectively aligned hierarchy of requirements and technical profiles; monitors and communicates across functional boundaries to meet project resource and quality expectations; ensures product capability meets or exceeds expectations and takes mitigating actions when project risks are higher than expected; understands the full product life cycle process and stakeholders. 

Product Failure Mode Avoidance - Mitigates potential product failure modes, by identifying interfaces, functions, functional requirements, interactions, control factors, noise factors, and prioritized potential failure modes and potential failure causes for the system of interest to effectively and efficiently improve the reliability of Cummins products. 

Product Function Modeling, Simulation and Analysis - Impacts product design decisions through the utilization and/or interpretation of computational tools and methods that predict the capability of a products function relative to its system, sub-system and/or component level requirements. 

Product Interface Management and Integration - Identifies and analyzes the interfaces and interactions across system boundaries by specifying the requirements and limits to ensure that the product meets requirements; controls the interactions across the system element boundaries by making sure that they remain within specified limits; integrates system elements by creating an integration plan, including identification of method and timing for each activity to make it easier to find, isolate, diagnose, and correct. 

Product Problem Solving - Solves product problems using a process that protects the customer; determines the assignable cause; implements robust, data-based solutions; and identifies the systemic root causes and recommended actions to prevent problem reoccurrence. 

Product Verification and Validation Management - Develops product systems validation plans from a variety of inputs to identify failure modes, while managing product risk and relative priority; negotiates product requirements against capability to guide project scope; evaluates analytical, simulation and physical test results to verify product capability and validate requirements; assesses legacy versus proposed system solution capabilities and produces recommendations with technical documentation to support product decisions. 

System Requirements Engineering - Uses appropriate methods and tools to translate stakeholder needs into verifiable requirements to which designs are developed; establishes acceptance criteria for the system of interest through analysis, allocation and negotiation; tracks the status of requirements throughout the system lifecycle; assesses the impact of changes to system requirements on project scope, schedule, and resources; creates and maintains information linkages to related artifacts. 

Technical Documentation - Documents information based on knowledge gained as part of technical function activities; communicates to stakeholders with the goal of enabling improved technical productivity and effective knowledge transfer to others who were not originally part of the initial learning. 

Technical Documentation - Documents information based on knowledge gained as part of technical function activities; communicates to stakeholders with the goal of enabling improved technical productivity and effective knowledge transfer to others who were not originally part of the initial learning. 

Builds networks - Effectively building formal and informal relationship networks inside and outside the organization. 

Communicates effectively - Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. 

Decision quality - Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward. 

Drives results - Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances. 

Manages complexity - Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems. 

Resourcefulness - Securing and deploying resources effectively and efficiently. 

Values differences - Recognizing the value that different perspectives and cultures bring to an organization. 

Design and Application of Open/Closed Loop Controls - Specifies software features that interact with mechanical, hydraulic, chemical and electronic systems to deliver desired system states; specifies control system architectures which include appropriate measurements, correct actuation, and algorithms for Cummins products; configures and/or understands open/closed loop feedback controls features and the system interactions between hardware and software in Cummins products. 

Product Configuration and Change Management - Establishes a baseline of identified product artifacts to be placed under configuration management; releases, tracks, controls and communicates changes from concept to obsolescence often through work requests; establishes and maintains the integrity of the product artifact baselines. 

Mechanical Design of Mechanical Systems - Acquires and applies an in-depth understanding of mechanical systems through working knowledge that guides a designer s ability to create innovative and sound design concepts to meet Cummins and customer expectations; designs for requirements of all lifecycle stages by considering the customer requirements in different operating environments to ensure a robust system. 

Mechanical Design Specification - Creates complete specifications in the form of solid models, configured engineering bill of materials and detailed drawings that cross-functionally communicate the information required to manufacture and inspect a product per its design intent; considers national, international, industry, and Cummins standards that accurately and concisely define the part specification. 

 Education, Licenses, Certifications: 
College, university, or equivalent Bachelors degree in Engineering or appropriate STEM field is required. 

Post-graduate (Masters) degree relevant to this discipline area may be required for select roles. 

This position may require licensing for compliance with export controls or sanctions regulations. 

 Experience: 
Prior Senior or Lead Engineer equivalent work experience in a relevant discipline area is required with a demonstrated track record of technical problem solving and quality decision making. Knowledge of MS Office tools is preferred.

title: Production and Supply Chain Coordinator
description:
Job Description: Production and Supply Chain Coordinator Location: Chakan, Pune, Maharashtra
 Department: Production / Supply Chain
 Experience: 6-9 Years
 Qualification: B.E. / B.Tech / Diploma in Mechanical or Production Engineering
 Preferred Industry: Pump Manufacturing, Valve Manufacturing, Process Equipment, Industrial Machinery 
 Contact :- 8855075289 -HR Share cv on :- recruiting@fristam.in 
 Job Summary We are looking for an experienced and proactive Production and Supply Chain Coordinator to manage end-to-end order planning, production coordination, material availability, inventory utilisation and on-time dispatch. The candidate will coordinate with Sales, Purchase, Production, Assembly, Stores and Quality teams to ensure customer orders are completed and dispatched within committed timelines. The role requires hands-on experience with SAP Business One (SAP B1) , Production Planning and Control (PPC), material planning and inventory management in a make-to-order manufacturing environment. Key Objective: Achieve the monthly production and dispatch plan while improving On-Time Delivery (OTD) and reducing order-to-dispatch lead time. 
 Key Responsibilities :- 
 1. Production Planning and On-Time Delivery Prepare monthly production and dispatch plans based on confirmed customer orders in coordination with Sales and the Plant Head. Monitor open customer orders and track committed delivery dates. Identify potential delays at least two weeks in advance and initiate corrective actions. Conduct daily shop-floor reviews and weekly plan-versus-actual meetings. Reprioritise production activities based on material availability, customer priorities and delivery commitments. Coordinate with Sales before communicating revised delivery dates to customers. 
 2. SAP Business One (SAP B1) and MIS Create, monitor and close Production Orders (MOs) within the defined timelines. Process production material issues and receipts accurately in SAP B1. Raise purchase requisitions based on MRP, production plans and material requirements. Ensure timely posting of Goods Receipt Notes (GRNs), inventory transfers and stock adjustments. Maintain accurate Bills of Materials (BOMs), routings and item master data in coordination with Engineering. Reconcile SAP inventory with physical stock and ensure timely closure of transactions at month-end. Prepare daily and weekly MIS reports covering order status, production progress, material shortages, WIP, OTD and dispatch performance. 
 3. Purchase and Supplier Coordination Follow up with suppliers for castings, machined components, motors, seals and other bought-out items. Track open Purchase Orders against required delivery dates. Expedite critical materials and escalate supplier delays with clear recovery plans. Coordinate with Purchase and Quality Control teams for incoming material inspection and timely material release. Prepare and circulate weekly material shortage reports linked to production orders. 
 4. Production and Assembly Coordination Coordinate with machining, assembly, testing, painting, packing and dispatch teams to ensure smooth workflow. Release production and assembly kits based on material availability to minimise incomplete jobs and work interruptions. Track Work in Progress (WIP) at each production stage. Coordinate final inspection, testing, documentation and dispatch activities. Resolve daily production bottlenecks in consultation with shop-floor supervisors. Ensure completed orders are dispatched as per the committed schedule. 
 5. Inventory and Material Planning Review available stock, slow-moving stock and non-moving inventory on a monthly basis. Utilise available inventory for open customer orders before initiating fresh purchase requisitions. Identify opportunities to utilise surplus stock through approved substitutes, alternate builds and standard sub-assemblies. Support the development of minimum and maximum stock levels for fast-moving standard components. Apply MRP, lead-time planning and inventory classification techniques to improve material availability and reduce lead times. 
 6. Performance Monitoring and Continuous Improvement Monitor monthly production plan achievement and On-Time Delivery (OTD). Analyse reasons for delayed orders and implement corrective and preventive actions. Track production efficiency, material shortages, WIP and dispatch plan versus actual performance. Identify process improvements to reduce manufacturing lead time, inventory holding and delivery delays. Drive accountability and coordination across internal departments to meet customer commitments. 
 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Monthly production plan achievement. On-Time Delivery (OTD) performance. Adherence to customer delivery commitments. Reduction in order-to-dispatch lead time. Material availability and reduction in production shortages. SAP B1 transaction accuracy and inventory reconciliation. Reduction in overdue production orders and WIP delays. Inventory utilisation and reduction in slow-moving/non-moving stock. Note: KPI targets will be finalised based on company requirements. 
 Required Qualifications and Experience :- 
 Education B.E. / B.Tech / Diploma in Mechanical Engineering or Production Engineering. MBA in Operations or Supply Chain Management will be an added advantage. 
 Experience 6-9 years of relevant experience in Production Planning and Control (PPC), production coordination, material planning or supply chain coordination. Experience in equipment manufacturing, preferably pumps, valves, process equipment, industrial machinery or similar industries. Experience working in a make-to-order or batch manufacturing environment is essential. 
 Mandatory Skills Hands-on experience with SAP Business One (SAP B1), including Production Orders, material issues and receipts, purchase requisitions, GRNs and inventory reports. Strong understanding of production planning, material requirement planning and shop-floor coordination. Ability to read and interpret BOMs and engineering drawings. Knowledge of machining, assembly and manufacturing processes. Strong MS Excel skills, including Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP and MIS reporting. Proven ability to coordinate with suppliers and cross-functional teams. Strong follow-up, problem-solving and delivery management skills. 
 Preferred Skills Exposure to castings, machined components, motors, seals and bought-out components. Knowledge of MRP, ABC/FSN inventory classification and lead-time planning. Experience handling export orders or orders requiring detailed technical and dispatch documentation. Experience improving inventory utilisation and reducing production lead times. 
 Desired Candidate Profile Strong ownership of production schedules and delivery commitments. Proactive in identifying and resolving material and production bottlenecks. Excellent coordination and follow-up skills. Clear communication skills in English, Hindi and Marathi. Ability to work under delivery pressure while maintaining accuracy and quality. 
 Interested candidates with relevant experience in equipment manufacturing and hands-on SAP Business One expertise are encouraged to apply.

title: Spare Parts Manager / Maintenance Inventory Manager
description:
1. Purpose of the Role: To ensure uninterrupted availability of spare parts, consumables, and maintenance materials for Forging, Machining, and Facility equipment by developing and managing an efficient maintenance inventory system. Responsible for spare parts planning, inventory optimization, procurement coordination, vendor management, warehouse control, and SAP inventory management to support plant reliability and operational excellence. 
 2. Responsibilities: a. Function Specific Manage end-to-end spare parts inventory for Forging, Machining, Utilities, and Facility equipment. Ensure availability of critical spare parts for production-critical machines and utilities. Develop and maintain spare parts inventory strategy based on equipment criticality and business risk. Classify spares into Critical, Insurance, Operational, and Consumable categories. Establish Min-Max stock levels and Reorder Point systems for all maintenance inventories. Monitor inventory levels and prevent stock-outs of critical items. Coordinate with Maintenance, Purchase, Production, and Finance departments for inventory planning. Maintain accurate spare part master data in SAP. Prepare annual spare parts budget and monitor inventory spending. Manage inventory valuation, stock turnover, and inventory optimization initiatives. Conduct critical spare part reviews with maintenance teams. Develop spare part standardization and interchangeability programs. Coordinate procurement of local and imported spare parts. Follow-up with OEMs and suppliers for timely delivery of critical items. Evaluate and develop alternate suppliers wherever possible. Monitor spare part consumption trends and forecast future requirements. Support preventive maintenance shutdowns through spare parts readiness. Conduct periodic stock verification and inventory audits. Ensure compliance with internal controls and inventory management procedures. Maintain spare part documentation, catalogues, drawings, technical specifications, and equipment BOMs. Support machine reliability programs through effective spare parts availability. Lead inventory reduction and cost optimization projects without affecting plant reliability. b. Key Equipment Coverage 1. Follow EHS guidelines for storage of oils, lubricants, chemicals, batteries, and hazardous materials. Maintain warehouse safety standards and housekeeping practices. Job Description - 
 Purchase Manager 

 Employee Name: Santosh pawar
 Company: Anjali T. Precision
 Position: Purchase Manager
 Department: Purchase
 Reporting To: Plant Head / Operations Head
 Location: Nighoje & Chikhali Unit 
 Employement Type: Full Time
 ______________________________________________________________________________________ 

 Position Summary 
The Purchase Head is responsible for leading and managing the organization's end-to-end procurement function by developing strategic sourcing plans, ensuring uninterrupted availability of raw materials, bought-out parts, consumables, tooling, capital equipment, services, and indirect materials required for manufacturing operations. The role is accountable for driving procurement excellence through effective supplier management, cost optimization, inventory planning, commercial negotiations, statutory compliance, and cross-functional collaboration.
The incumbent shall establish robust procurement processes, strengthen supplier relationships, improve procurement efficiency, and ensure the achievement of Quality, Cost, and Delivery (QCD) objectives. The Purchase Head is also responsible for leading the purchase team, monitoring departmental KPIs, implementing digital task management practices, and supporting continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational performance and business profitability.

 Key Roles & Responsibilities 
 1. Procurement Strategy & Planning 
 Develop and implement procurement strategies aligned with the company's business objectives and operational requirements. Prepare annual procurement plans, sourcing strategies, and departmental budgets. Ensure uninterrupted availability of raw materials, bought-out parts, consumables, tooling, capital equipment, maintenance spares, and indirect materials. Establish procurement plans based on production forecasts, inventory levels, and customer demand. Drive strategic sourcing initiatives to improve procurement efficiency and supply chain reliability. Support business expansion through effective procurement planning and supplier development. 
 2. Vendor Development & Supplier Management 
 Identify, evaluate, qualify, and approve new suppliers based on Quality, Cost, Delivery, and Technical Capability. Build long-term strategic relationships with key suppliers. Conduct supplier audits, capability assessments, and performance reviews. Monitor supplier performance using predefined KPIs and implement corrective actions where required. Lead supplier development initiatives to improve quality, delivery performance, responsiveness, and cost competitiveness. Resolve supplier-related quality, delivery, and commercial issues in coordination with internal stakeholders. 
 3. Purchase Operations & Material Procurement 
 Oversee procurement of all direct and indirect materials required for manufacturing operations. Ensure timely release and follow-up of Purchase Orders (POs). Monitor order acknowledgements, supplier commitments, and delivery schedules. Coordinate with PPC, Production, Stores, Quality, Maintenance, NPD, and Finance to ensure smooth material flow. Ensure critical materials are available to avoid production interruptions. Monitor procurement lead times and expedite urgent material requirements whenever necessary. Ensure adherence to approved procurement procedures and authorization matrices. 
 4. Commercial Negotiation & Cost Management 
 Lead commercial negotiations for pricing, payment terms, delivery schedules, warranty conditions, and contractual obligations. Develop and implement annual cost reduction and value engineering initiatives. Analyse market trends, commodity prices, and raw material fluctuations to support strategic sourcing decisions. Identify opportunities for supplier consolidation and procurement optimization. Achieve cost savings without compromising product quality or delivery performance. Monitor procurement budgets and control overall purchasing expenditure. 
 5. Contract Management & Compliance 
 Finalize supplier contracts, annual rate agreements, and long-term supply agreements. Ensure all commercial agreements comply with company policies and statutory regulations. Maintain procurement documentation in accordance with ISO 9001, IATF 16949, and internal quality management systems. Ensure compliance with applicable legal, environmental, and ethical procurement standards. Support internal, customer, and external audits by maintaining complete procurement records and documentation. 
 6. Inventory & Supply Chain Coordination 
 Monitor inventory levels and procurement schedules to maintain optimum stock levels. Coordinate closely with Stores to minimize excess inventory while preventing stock-outs. Review slow-moving, non-moving, and obsolete inventory and initiate corrective actions. Collaborate with PPC and Production to align procurement with manufacturing schedules. Improve inventory turnover through effective procurement planning. 
 7. Cross-Functional Coordination 
 Work closely with PPC, Production, Stores, Quality Assurance, Finance, NPD, Maintenance, HR, and Operations to ensure smooth procurement operations. Support new product development by sourcing new materials, components, and suppliers. Participate in cross-functional meetings to resolve supply chain challenges. Ensure effective communication between suppliers and internal departments. 
 8. Team Leadership & Performance Management 
 Lead, mentor, and develop the Purchase Department team. Allocate responsibilities and monitor workload distribution. Establish departmental objectives, KPIs, and performance targets. Conduct periodic performance reviews and provide coaching for continuous improvement. Identify training needs and support employee skill development. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning. 
 9. MIS, Reporting & Performance Monitoring 
 Prepare and present daily, weekly, and monthly procurement reports to management. Monitor procurement KPIs and supplier performance metrics. Analyse procurement data to identify cost-saving opportunities and operational improvements. Prepare monthly purchase budget reports and cost-saving analysis. Track procurement lead times, supplier delivery performance, and purchasing efficiency. Maintain accurate procurement records and dashboards for management review. 
 10. Digital Task Management & Reporting 
The Purchase Head shall ensure disciplined implementation of digital task management and performance reporting across the Purchase Department.
 Responsibilities 
 Use Microsoft Planner daily to plan, assign, monitor, and review all departmental procurement activities. Review all assigned tasks at the beginning of each working day and ensure timely completion within defined deadlines. Assign and delegate procurement activities to Purchase Managers, Purchase Engineers, Buyers, and departmental team members through Microsoft Planner. Monitor task progress, follow up on pending activities, and ensure timely closure of all assigned tasks. Update task status with appropriate remarks, supporting documents, and completion evidence. Conduct daily Planner review meetings with the purchase team to monitor operational progress. Escalate overdue or delayed procurement activities to the Operations Head along with corrective action plans. Fill and review the Daily Progress Report in the designated Google Sheet before the end of every working day. Ensure all completed work, pending purchase orders, supplier follow-ups, delivery delays, commercial issues, and action plans are accurately recorded. Maintain complete transparency, accountability, and digital tracking of all procurement activities. 
 11. Continuous Improvement 
 Drive Lean Procurement and continuous improvement initiatives. Identify opportunities to automate procurement processes and improve operational efficiency. Standardize procurement procedures and documentation. Reduce procurement cycle time and improve supplier responsiveness. Promote innovation, value engineering, and strategic sourcing practices to enhance business competitiveness. 
 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) 
 Operational KPIs 
 Purchase Cost Savings Supplier On-Time Delivery (OTD) Supplier Quality Performance (PPM) Procurement Lead Time Purchase Order Cycle Time Inventory Optimisation Vendor Development Purchase Budget Compliance Material Availability for Production Emergency Purchase Reduction Financial KPIs 
 Annual Cost Reduction Procurement Budget Adherence Cost Avoidance Through Negotiation Inventory Carrying Cost Reduction Digital KPIs 
 100% Microsoft Planner Compliance On-Time Task Completion Task Delegation Effectiveness Daily Google Sheet Reporting Compliance Departmental Task Closure Rate Compliance KPIs 
 ISO & IATF Compliance Supplier Audit Compliance Procurement Documentation Accuracy Zero Procurement Policy Violations 
 Educational Qualification 
 Bachelor's Degree or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or a related discipline. MBA in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, or Materials Management will be preferred. 
 Experience 
 1218 years of experience in manufacturing procurement, sourcing, and supply chain management. Minimum 5 years of experience in a leadership role managing procurement teams. The Store Manager will be responsible for managing and controlling the companys inventory, raw materials, finished goods, consumables, and spare parts to ensure smooth production operations. The role includes maintaining accurate stock records, monitoring inventory levels, supervising store staff, and ensuring proper material movement, storage, and documentation in accordance with company policies and quality standards.

 Key Roles & Responsibilities 
 1. Inventory Management 
 Maintain accurate inventory records of raw materials, WIP, finished goods, and consumables . Monitor minimum stock levels, reorder levels, and safety stock . Conduct regular physical stock verification and cycle counting . Ensure stock accuracy in ERP or inventory management system . 2. Material Receiving & Storage

 Issue materials to production based on authorized requisitions . Ensure timely availability of materials to avoid production downtime . Maintain proper documentation of material movement . 4. Inventory Control & Optimization 
 Track slow-moving, non-moving, and obsolete inventory . Implement strategies to reduce excess inventory and improve inventory turnover . Monitor material consumption and coordinate with Purchase & PPC departments . 5. Store Organization & Safety 
 Maintain 5S standards in the store area . Ensure proper material handling, storage racks, and safety compliance . Implement FIFO / FEFO inventory practices . 6. Documentation & Reporting 
 Maintain accurate records of: GRN Material Issue Notes Stock Registers Inventory Reports 
 Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly stock reports for management. 7. Team Management 
 Supervise and guide store assistants and store operators . Ensure discipline, training, and productivity within the stores department. 8. Audit & Compliance 
 Support internal and external audits related to stores and inventory. Ensure compliance with company procedures, ISO standards, and inventory policies .

Testing and Quality Assurance: Contribute to model calibration by adjusting input parameters and aligning outputs with historical data benchmarks. Testing and Quality Assurance: Conduct regular quality checks on input data and model assumptions to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with industry standards. Address data discrepancies and coordinate with relevant team members to resolve any data-related issues. description:
Job Title: Senior Executive/Assistant Manager - Supply Chain Management (SCM) Department: Supply Chain Management / Planning Reports To: Head - Planning Location: Chakan, Pune Employment Type: Full-Time Grade/Level: Assistant Manager Job Purpose This position is responsible for supply planning, coordinating Drug Product (DP) filling schedules, and packing material planning, to ensure uninterrupted production, packing, and dispatch timelines. The role requires close coordination with Production, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Warehouse, Procurement, and Finance functions, and works within the framework of cGMP and applicable regulatory requirements. Key Responsibilities 1. Supply Planning - Prepare and maintain rolling supply plans (monthly/quarterly) for DP filling and packing operations in line with sales forecast, production capacity, and inventory targets. - Participate in Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) discussions; provide inputs on DP filling and packing material readiness against the demand plan. - Monitor supply-demand gaps for critical raw materials, packing materials, and filling capacity; highlight risks and propose mitigation plans. - Coordinate with Production, Procurement, and Logistics to align supply plans with material availability and dispatch schedules. - Maintain safety stock/buffer norms for critical packing materials and components to safeguard against supply disruptions. - Track plan-versus-actual performance (fill rate, schedule adherence) and drive corrective actions for deviations. - Support annual budgeting and capacity planning exercises with supply-side inputs. - Prepare and circulate periodic supply planning reports/dashboards to the Head - Planning and senior management. 2. DP (Drug Product) Filling - Planning & Coordination - Prepare, update, and maintain DP filling schedules in coordination with Production, QA, and QC to meet batch release and dispatch timelines. - Track filling line capacity and utilization; proactively flag risks of schedule slippage and coordinate re-planning with stakeholders. - Liaise with Production and Warehouse teams to ensure timely availability of drug substance, components, and consumables required for filling batches. - Monitor batch progress against the plan and circulate daily/weekly status updates to the Head - Planning and cross-functional teams. - Coordinate with QA on batch documentation, release timelines, and any deviations affecting the filling plan. - Support capacity planning and scheduling for new products/technology transfers on the filling line. 3. Packing Material Planning & Procurement - Plan and procure primary and secondary packing materials (vials, stoppers, seals/caps, cartons, labels, package inserts, shippers, etc.) in line with production plans and inventory norms. - Identify, evaluate, and develop reliable vendors for packing materials; negotiate pricing, lead times, and payment terms. - Release and follow up purchase orders; track vendor delivery performance and resolve supply escalations. - Maintain optimum inventory levels of packing materials to avoid stock-outs or excess inventory; monitor min-max/safety stock levels and reorder points. - Coordinate with QA and Warehouse for incoming material inspection, approval, and handling of deviations/rejections. - Ensure procurement activities comply with cGMP, vendor qualification, and applicable regulatory documentation requirements. 4. Cross-Functional Coordination & Reporting - Work closely with Production, QA, QC, Warehouse, Procurement, and Finance to ensure smooth material flow, invoice processing, and payment closure. - Maintain accurate MIS/trackers for supply plans, DP filling schedules, and packing material stock and procurement status. - Support internal, customer, and regulatory audits with relevant SCM documentation and records. - Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance planning accuracy, vendor reliability, and procurement cost efficiency. - Escalate critical supply or schedule risks to the Head - Planning in a timely manner. Qualification & Experience - Graduate / B.Pharm (M.Pharm or MBA in Operations/Supply Chain Management preferred). - 4-6 years of relevant experience in supply chain, supply planning, and/or procurement, preferably within a pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical manufacturing environment. - Prior exposure to injectable/Drug Product (DP) filling operations and packing material procurement will be an added advantage. Key Skills & Competencies - Working knowledge of cGMP, regulatory, and quality requirements applicable to pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical manufacturing. - Proficiency in ERP systems (SAP or similar) and MS Excel for supply planning, procurement, and inventory tracking. - Strong analytical and forecasting skills for supply-demand planning. - Strong vendor management, negotiation, and commercial acumen. - Effective cross-functional coordination and communication skills. - Ability to work under tight timelines in a dynamic manufacturing environment. Reporting Relationship - Reports To: Head - Planning - This role does not currently have direct reportees.

Key Skills: SAP,Biopharma,Sales,Injectables,Inventory management,SCM,Management,CGMP

title: Purchase, Category & Sourcing Executive
description:
1. Product Selection & Category Building 
 Recommend which products and brands CIY should keep, add or remove based on sales data, customer demand, store feedback and seasonal trends. Find new products in craft, art, hobby, stationery, gifting, sewing, beads, yarn and related categories. Help build better product ranges for store shelves and online. 
 
 2. Own-Brand Product Development (strategic priority) 
 Help CIY source products to be sold under the CIY own brand this is a key growth lever for the business. Drive sample follow-up, costing, packaging coordination and supplier comparison. Identify products with strong demand and healthy margin potential. Work under founder guidance for final product decisions, but bring strong sourcing options to the table. 
 
 3. Buying & Reordering 
 Check sales and stock every week. Prepare reorder plans for fast-selling products. Keep top-selling products in stock above 95% of the time. Avoid overbuying products that may not sell. Follow up with suppliers until products are received and ready to sell. 
 
 4. Supplier & Factory Sourcing 
 Find new suppliers, wholesalers and direct factories. Compare prices, quality, delivery time and payment terms. Negotiate better buying prices and terms. Build backup supplier options for important products. Visit local markets and suppliers regularly. Expect 12 days per week of field work in Pune; occasional travel to Mumbai or Delhi for trade shows. 
 
 5. Pricing & Profit 
 Check buying price, transport cost, packaging cost and selling price before purchase. Help set prices that are competitive but still profitable. Suggest bundles, offers and discount ideas to clear slow stock. Avoid buying decisions that block cash or reduce profit. 
 
 6. Slow Stock Control 
 Track products that are not selling. Suggest action: bundle, discount, better display, online push, return to supplier or stop reordering. Work with the store team to improve visibility of slow products. Reduce old stock month by month. 
 
 7. Store & Online Coordination 
 Walk the store regularly and speak to the store team. Understand what customers are asking for what is selling, what is stuck, what is missing. Coordinate with the online team for correct product names, prices, photos and details. Make sure ordered stock, received stock and supplier bills match before closing purchases. 
 
 Daily & Weekly Work 
 Check sales and current stock daily. Make reorder lists and place purchase orders after approval. Follow up with suppliers for delivery and resolve issues. Compare supplier rates regularly; benchmark existing vendors against new quotes. Visit markets and suppliers 12 days per week. Walk the store at least twice a week to spot stockouts and slow movers. Share a weekly report: what sold well, what is out of stock, what was ordered, what is stuck and what action is needed next. 
 
 What Success Looks Like 
 Top-selling products stay in stock above 95% of the time. Slow and old stock reduces every month. Buying prices improve over time; supplier payment terms get more favourable. Supplier delivery becomes faster and more reliable. Store team gets the right products at the right time. CIY own-brand products move from idea to sample to store shelf. Purchase decisions become planned, not last-minute. 
 
 Who Should Apply 
 You should apply if you are: Practical, fast and reliable. Good with numbers and simple spreadsheets. Strong in follow-up you finish what you start. Comfortable talking to and negotiating with suppliers in Hindi, Marathi or basic English. Willing to do field work and market visits this is not a desk-only role. Able to think like a business owner, not just an employee. Interested in products, retail, craft, design, stationery, fashion accessories, gifting or home products. 
 
 Experience Required 
 Minimum 1 year and up to 4 years of experience in purchase, retail buying, merchandising, sourcing, supplier management, retail operations or wholesale market work. Hands-on experience running a family business, working in a wholesale market, or actively trading and reselling products counts as relevant experience tell us about it in your answers. Pure academic backgrounds without practical street experience will not be considered for this role. 
 
 Skills Needed 
 Google Sheets or Excel. Basic maths: price, quantity, margin, discount and transport cost. Supplier negotiation. Product comparison and market research. Follow-up and execution. Clear communication in Hindi and basic English. Marathi is a strong plus. 
 
 Good to Have 
 Experience in art, craft, stationery, fabric, yarn, beads, gifting, fashion accessories or home products. Knowledge of Pune local wholesale markets (Budhwar Peth, Laxmi Road) or Mumbai (Crawford Market, Bhuleshwar). Experience with Shopify, Zoho or any inventory software. Personal interest in DIY, craft, knitting, crochet, sewing, painting, jewellery making or creative products. 
 
 Performance Will Be Measured On 
 Availability of top-selling products: 95% in-stock target. Reduction in old and slow stock month over month. Improvement in buying rates and supplier payment terms. On-time supplier delivery rate. Accuracy and speed of reorder planning. Own-brand product progress samples to shelves. Clean and current purchase and supplier data.

title: Unit Manager - Digital Platforms and Consumer AI/Senior Unit Manager
description:
Job Summary 
 At Bajaj Finance, we help millions of people across India manage their money. People come to us when they want to buy a new phone on EMI, when they need a personal loan for a wedding, when they want to buy insurance, or when they want to grow their savings in a Fixed Deposit. Because we have so many customers, we get thousands of questions every single day. Customers want to know their account balance. They want to change the date their EMI gets deducted. They want to know the fees for closing a loan early. In the past, to get these answers, a customer had to wait on hold to talk to a call center agent, or they had to tap through ten different screens on our mobile app. We want to change that. We want to make it as easy as sending a text message to a friend. We are building a massive, highly intelligent AI (Artificial Intelligence) platform. Think of it like a super-smart chat assistant built right into the Bajaj Finance app. We want our customers to be able to just type out their problems in plain English, Hindi, or other languages, and have the AI fix the problem instantly. If a customer types, "Hey, I need to pause my loan payment this month," the AI should understand them, check their account, and do the work in seconds. Building this is incredibly hard. It is not just a simple robot that gives canned answers. It is a smart system that has to understand human language, connect to our deep banking systems, and follow strict financial rules. 

 Responsibilities 
 As a Product Manager, you will read these PPG rulebooks. You will pull out all the rules related to your project. You will work with the engineers to make sure these rules are permanently locked into the AI's brain. If the company changes a rule in the PPG next year, you are the person who makes sure the AI gets updated immediately. Synthetic Testing: Once the engineers build a version of the AI, we have to test it. But we cannot let a broken, untested AI talk to real Bajaj Finance customers. That is too risky. If the AI is confused, a real customer might get bad advice about their loan. So, we use something called Synthetic Testing. "Synthetic" just means fake or made-up. You will help create thousands of fake conversations to test the AI safely. You will create fake customer profiles. For example, you make a fake customer named Rahul who has a home loan. You will type to the AI pretending to be Rahul. You will ask, "Can I pay off my whole loan today" and see what the AI says. Does the AI say yesDoes it calculate the early payment fee correctlyWhat if you pretend to be a customer who types with terrible spellingWhat if you type in a mix of Hindi and EnglishWhat if you pretend to be very angryDoes the AI still understand and stay politeYou will run hundreds of these fake tests. When the AI fails, you write down why it failed, take that information back to the engineers, and tell them what to fix. You keep doing this until the AI passes every fake test perfectly. LLM Parameters (What We Send to the AI Brain): The core brain of our AI is called a Large Language Model (LLM). Think of the LLM like an incredibly smart person sitting in a dark room. This person knows how to speak perfectly, but they have no idea who they are talking to. If a customer types, "What is my balance", the smart person in the dark room has no idea whose balance to check. So, we have to send the LLM a package of extra information along with the customer's question. We call this setting the LLM Parameters. As the Product Manager, you will decide exactly what information goes into that package. When the customer asks about their balance, you will tell our computer systems: "Before you let the AI answer, grab the customer's name, grab their last three payments, and grab their current loan amount. Send all of that to the AI." You also have to send strict instructions. You will tell the AI, "You are a helpful assistant for Bajaj Finance. Always be polite. Do not guess numbers. Only use the numbers I just sent you." If you send the AI too much information, it gets confused and it costs the company too much money to process. If you send too little information, the AI gives a stupid answer. Your job is to find the perfect balance of what data to send the AI every time a customer speaks. Visualisations: Chatting with an AI should not just be reading massive blocks of text. Nobody wants to read a giant paragraph of words on their small phone screen. Sometimes, the best way to answer a customer is by showing them a picture, a chart, or a button. We call these Visualisations. Let\'s say a customer asks, "How much of my loan have I paid off" The AI could write a long, boring sentence with a bunch of numbers. But it is much better if the AI shows a nice, clean pie chart on the screen. Half the pie is green for the money paid, and half is grey for the money left. The customer understands it instantly. Or, if the AI needs the customer to pick a date, it shouldn\'t make the customer type "October 15th." It should pop up a small calendar on the screen so the customer can just tap the day. You will decide when to use text and when to use these visual tools. You will work with our designers to sketch out how these charts and buttons should look so the chat is beautiful and easy to use. Product Switching: Imagine you are talking to a human salesman at a store. You ask about buying a TV. Then, suddenly, you change your mind and ask about buying a fridge. The human easily switches the topic to the fridge.Computers are not naturally good at this. If the computer is programmed to talk to you about a TV, and you ask about a fridge, the computer will get totally confused. It might say, "Error, I do not understand." At Bajaj Finance, we have dozens of products. A customer might start a chat asking about their EMI shopping card. But halfway through the chat, they might say, "By the way, I also want to open a Fixed Deposit." The AI needs to smoothly switch from talking about the shopping card to talking about the Fixed Deposit without breaking or crashing. We call this Product Switching. You will write the rules for how the AI handles these sudden changes in conversation. You will plan out how the AI remembers what the customer was talking about first, just in case the customer wants to go back to the original topic later. Conversation Flows: A normal conversation flows naturally. But computers need a map. They need to be told exactly how a conversation should go, step by step. You will create these maps, which we call Conversation Flows. You will literally use a software tool to draw boxes and arrows on your screen. 
Box 1: The AI says, "Hello, how can I help" -> Arrow points to Box 2. 
Box 2: The customer says, "I want to see my statement." -> Arrow points to Box 3. 
Box 3: The system checks if the customer\'s phone number is verified. 
If Yes -> Arrow points to Box 4. 
If No -> Arrow points to Box 5. 
Box 4: Show the statement on the screen. 
Box 5: Ask the customer to type in a one-time password (OTP). You have to map out every single path the conversation could possibly take. You have to think of all the "what ifs." What if the customer types the wrong password What if the customer stops replying and walks away from their phone What if the internet crashes You must draw a box and an arrow for every single situation. These flowcharts become the actual instruction manual for the engineers. They look at your map and write

title: Systems Engineering Professional
description:
Systems Engineer Robotics & Automation Work Location Pune Work Mode In Campus Department Systems Engineering Employment Type Full-Time Reporting To Head of Systems Engineering Experience 3-6 years 
 ABOUT US Unbox Robotics is a deep-tech robotics company building the worlds most space-efficient warehouse sorting systems. Our swarm robotics platform - UnboxSort - enables e-commerce, retail, and 3PL operators to sort at 3-5 the throughput of conventional systems, in a fraction of the floor space. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Pune, we operate across 20+ sites in 9 countries, serving leading players in e-commerce, retail, CEP, and 3PL across India, Europe, and the USA. Series B funded, we are scaling rapidly toward our next phase of global growth. We believe great robots are built on rigorous engineering - and Systems Engineering is where that rigour begins. 
 ROLE OVERVIEW Own the definition, integration, and validation of a robotic subsystem or an end-to-end function. Your scope could include motion execution, sensing, robot-to-server communication, charging, or fault recovery. You will translate operational needs into specifications, maintain interfaces across engineering teams, and demonstrate that the delivered function meets its performance, reliability, and cost targets. Success in this role means your subsystem has an agreed operational purpose, clear requirements, controlled interfaces, and complete acceptance evidence - with documents and the implemented system staying aligned as changes occur, and manufacturing and field teams able to reproduce expected performance and diagnose failures. 
 ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES Operational Definition & Specifications Contribute to the system Concept of Operations (ConOps) and develop detailed scenarios for your scope, including startup, normal operation, shutdown, maintenance, failures, and recovery Author and maintain assigned portions of the System Specification Document (SSD) and the complete specifications for your subsystem or function Define measurable requirements, constraints, assumptions, and acceptance criteria Functional Design & Interfaces Develop functional breakdowns, state machines, sequence diagrams, and subsystem design descriptions with the relevant engineering teams Own Interface Control Documents (ICDs) for your scope, defining applicable mechanical and electrical interfaces, signals, units, coordinate frames, message formats, timing, timeouts, and compatibility requirements Engineering Trade-offs & Integration Analyse accuracy, latency, bandwidth, power, compute, and component-cost requirements, and validate assumptions through calculations and physical measurements Plan bring-up and integration activities, resolve dependencies, and maintain a reproducible configuration across hardware, firmware, and software Verification & Validation Author and execute plans that demonstrate compliance with requirements and suitability for intended operating scenarios Select appropriate simulation, replay, bench, hardware-in-the-loop, and robot tests Failure Behaviour & Change Control Work with domain engineers to define detection, degraded operation, recovery, and diagnostics Lead investigations across hardware and software boundaries and verify corrective actions Assess changes against requirements, interfaces, risks, and existing test evidence; maintain traceability and bring proposed changes through technical review Production & Field Feedback Support calibration procedures, manufacturing acceptance tests, pilot deployments, and improvements based on operational data 
 Engineering Deliverables You Will Own Subsystem specifications and assigned system-level requirements ConOps contributions, functional diagrams, and operating-state descriptions ICDs and subsystem design descriptions Performance budgets and documented trade studies Verification and validation plans, traceability records, and acceptance reports Change-impact assessments and investigation reports 
 REQUIREMENTS Must Have Experience delivering a robotic, embedded, automation, or electromechanical subsystem into real operation Technical depth in at least one discipline, and the ability to reason across mechanics, electronics, controls, firmware, and software Demonstrated ability to write testable requirements and useful interface specifications Experience using calculations, logs, controlled experiments, and instrumentation to identify root causes Python or comparable scripting proficiency, with the ability to understand relevant embedded or robotics software Working knowledge of communication interfaces and timing behaviour in embedded or distributed systems Ability to lead technical reviews and take an ambiguous problem through to a verified outcome 
 Good to Have Mobile robots and fleet coordination Calibration and control-system characterisation Automated testing Failure-mode analysis Manufacturing test Requirements-management tools Industrial deployments 
 ELIGIBLE CANDIDATES Desired Qualification Relevant engineering education or equivalent practical experience 
 Work Experience 3-6 years delivering robotic, embedded, automation, or electromechanical subsystems 
 WE VALUE Ownership - carries a subsystem from definition through to field performance Clarity - writes requirements and interfaces others can build and test against Evidence-Based Decisions - backs trade-offs with calculations, logs, and measurements Cross-Disciplinary Thinking - reasons across mechanics, electronics, controls, firmware, and software Closure on Ambiguity - turns open-ended problems into verified outcomes 
 WHY JOIN US Own a real piece of a robotic platform that runs in live warehouses. Your specifications, interfaces, and acceptance evidence will directly determine how reliably Unbox Robotics fleets perform at customer sites across India, Europe, and the USA. 
 You won t just own a subsystem. You ll own the proof that it works - in the warehouse, at scale. 
 Work Location: Pune Work Mode: In Campus Salary Range: Competitive Salary

Project Controls & Reporting Maintain commercial dashboards, action registers, variation logs, claim trackers, and procurement compliance reports. title: Supplier Quality Manager 4
description:
In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Be: Lead supplier development strategies and initiatives that improve supplier capability, capacity, quality, delivery performance, innovation, safety, and cash optimization. Partner with Product Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Operations, and Sourcing teams to execute supplier development projects that align with business objectives and growth priorities. Drive successful implementation of new product introduction, localization, supplier transitions, and supply chain risk mitigation initiatives. Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders to enhance collaboration, responsiveness, and overall supply chain performance. Champion a proactive safety culture by promoting compliance with safety standards and best practices across the supplier network. Monitor supplier performance using key operational and quality metrics and identify opportunities for continuous improvement. Assess supplier capabilities and performance gaps, develop improvement plans, and track progress against defined milestones and objectives. Facilitate supplier participation in new product development activities, project reviews, qualification programs, and business growth initiatives. Collaborate with suppliers and cross-functional teams to analyze demand forecasts, evaluate production capacity, and ensure continuity of supply. Drive adoption of structured problem-solving, Lean principles, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement methodologies. Support supplier education and capability-building programs that enable sustainable operational excellence. Coordinate First Article Inspection activities and ensure timely completion of qualification requirements for development and sourcing projects. Lead implementation and compliance activities related to Production Part Approval Process requirements where applicable. Evaluate supplier manufacturing readiness, scalability, and operational effectiveness to support current and future business needs. Identify potential supply chain risks and implement mitigation plans that support business continuity and customer satisfaction. Drive supplier consolidation and optimization strategies by strengthening relationships with high-performing suppliers and identifying new sourcing opportunities. Deliver measurable improvements in quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, and supplier responsiveness across the supply base. Who You Are: 
 You build strong partnerships and work collaboratively across functions, suppliers, and regions to achieve shared objectives. You make sound decisions by analyzing information, evaluating risks, and balancing short-term priorities with long-term business goals. You actively seek opportunities to improve processes, challenge conventional approaches, and drive innovative solutions that enhance performance. You develop effective plans, maintain accountability for results, and adapt to changing business needs while helping others succeed through clear communication, influence, and collaboration. For This Role, You Will Need: Experience leading supplier development, supplier performance improvement, or supply chain optimization initiatives in a manufacturing environment. Knowledge of supplier quality systems, manufacturing processes, and supply chain management principles. Experience working with machined, molded, and purchased components or comparable manufacturing categories. Ability to evaluate supplier capability, capacity, performance, and operational readiness. Experience leading cross-functional projects involving sourcing, operations, engineering, quality, and supply chain teams. Understanding of continuous improvement methodologies, structured problem-solving approaches, and root cause analysis techniques. Ability to analyze data, identify trends, and translate insights into actionable improvement plans. Strong communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and relationship-building skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic global business environment. Willingness and ability to travel as required to supplier and business locations. Preferred Qualifications That Set You Apart: Experience supporting new product introduction, supplier transitions, localization programs, or strategic sourcing initiatives. Knowledge of APQP, PPAP, First Article Inspection requirements, and supplier qualification processes. Experience implementing Lean Manufacturing, operational excellence, or continuous improvement programs within supplier networks. Knowledge of supply risk management, supplier development frameworks, and global sourcing strategies. Experience working within a multinational manufacturing organization and collaborating with geographically dispersed teams. Professional certifications related to quality, operations, supply chain, or continuous improvement are valued. Demonstrated success achieving measurable improvements in supplier quality, on-time delivery, productivity, and cost performance. Our Culture and Commitment To You: 
 At Emerson, we prioritize a workplace where every employee is valued, respected, and empowered to grow. We foster an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, and diverse perspectives-because we know that great ideas come from great teams. Our commitment to ongoing career development and growing an inclusive culture ensures you have the support to thrive. Whether through mentorship, training, or leadership opportunities, we invest in your success so you can make a lasting impact. We believe diverse teams working together are key to driving growth and delivering business results.

Job Summary We are seeking an experienced SAP PPDS (Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling) Consultant to support the design, configuration, implementation, and optimization of SAP PPDS solutions. The ideal candidate will have strong functional expertise in production planning, detailed scheduling, master data management, planning engines, and SAP manufacturing processes. The consultant will be responsible for gathering business requirements, conducting fit-gap analysis, configuring SAP PPDS, preparing functional specifications, supporting testing activities, and managing deployment and post-go-live support. The role requires close collaboration with business stakeholders and technical teams to deliver effective, scalable, and optimized production planning solutions throughout the project lifecycle. Key Responsibilities Gather, analyze, and document business requirements related to production planning and detailed scheduling. Conduct fit-gap analysis to identify standard SAP capabilities, process gaps, and required custom developments. Configure SAP PPDS based on business requirements and prepare functional specifications for custom enhancements. Participate in all testing phases, including unit testing, integration testing, regression testing, and user acceptance testing (UAT). Collaborate with clients, business users, functional teams, and technical teams to resolve issues and ensure successful project delivery. Support cutover planning, deployment, Go-Live, and post-Go-Live hypercare activities. Configure and validate SAP PPDS master data, including products, locations, resources, Production Data Structures (PDS), transportation lanes, models, and versions. Manage and troubleshoot transactional data, including planned orders, production orders, stock transport requisitions (STRs), and stock transport orders (STOs). Understand and manage pegging relationships between supply and demand elements. Configure and utilize PPDS planning engines, including heuristics and the optimizer, to support production planning and scheduling requirements. Implement and support setup optimization, block planning, and campaign planning processes. Configure and support Make-to-Stock (MTS) and Make-to-Order (MTO) planning strategies within SAP PPDS. description:
About the Role The Lead Electrical & Instrumentation will oversee the complete E&I engineering scope across all phases of the Blue hydrogen and Ammonia projectfrom concept and pre-bid engineering to detailed design, procurement support, installation, testing, and commissioning. The incumbent will ensure all electrical and instrumentation systems are designed, engineered, and executed in compliance with project requirements, statutory norms, safety standards, and industry best practices. This role demands strong technical leadership, interdisciplinary coordination, and the ability to manage multiple stakeholders, vendors, and project interfaces. Key Responsibilities 1. Pre-Bid & Conceptual Engineering Lead E&I inputs for pre-bid and conceptual design, including system sizing, specification preparation, power load estimation, instrumentation architecture, and BOQ development. Review client specifications, standards, and project requirements and prepare technical clarifications for bid submissions. 2. Detailed Engineering Manage the development and review of all discipline-specific engineering deliverables including: Single Line Diagrams (SLDs) Cable Schedules Load Lists Equipment Specifications & Datasheets Control & Instrumentation Layouts Loop Diagrams Cause & Effect Diagrams Hook-up drawings Ensure E&I designs comply with functional, process, and performance requirements. Review and approve vendor drawings, engineering documents, and FAT procedures. 3. Procurement & Vendor Coordination Prepare technical specifications, RFQs, and evaluation sheets for E&I equipment such as: Power Transformers, Switchgear, PCCs, MCCs, UPS, motors. Substation, battery systems, grounding systems. Electrical protection systems, Arc-flash analysis. PLC/DCS systems, Analyzers, field instruments. Control valves, Shutdown valves, Blowdown and safety systems. HT & LT Cables, junction boxes, control panels. Support technical bid evaluations, vendor selection, and engineering clarifications. Coordinate FATs, inspections, and quality checks with vendors. Define control logic, alarm philosophy, interlock design, and functional safety (SIL) assessments in line with IEC 61511. 4. Installation, Testing & Commissioning Provide technical oversight during installation and commissioning of E&I systems. Resolve site engineering issues and ensure adherence to approved drawings and standards. Support SAT, loop checking, control logic testing, and system energization. 5. Standards, Codes & Compliance Ensure designs comply with relevant codes and standards including: IEC, IEEE, NEC, IS, NFPA, ANSI, ISA, API, ASME Electrical safety and arc-flash protection standards Hazardous area classification (ATEX, IECEx) Ensure all E&I systems meet statutory, environmental, and regulatory compliance as per US norms. 6. Cross-Discipline Coordination Coordinate closely with process, mechanical, civil, and HSE disciplines to ensure total system integration. Participate in design reviews, HAZOP, SIL studies, model reviews, and constructability assessments. Provide technical support for resolving interdisciplinary issues. 7. Project Controls & Documentation Identify E&I deliverables and ensure timely preparation and submission. Track progress, highlight delays, and support corrective actions. Ensure strict adherence to quality standards, engineering processes, and project schedules. 8. Safety & Reliability Ensure electrical and instrumentation systems are designed for safe operation, reliability, and maintainability. Support development of grounding, lightning protection, and safety interlock systems. Drive implementation of best practices for electrical safety and instrumentation integrity.

Ensure proper operation, maintenance, and availability of laboratory equipment. Maintain laboratory discipline, 5S, and workflow efficiency. Calibration & Laboratory Equipment Control Prepare and maintain the laboratory calibration plan. Ensure timely calibration of all measuring and testing equipment. Identify equipment requiring repair, replacement, or external calibration. Ensure no expired or out-of-calibration equipment is used for product acceptance testing. F. Coordinate customer-specific testing and qualification programs. Support product approval and qualification activities. Participate in technical discussions with customers when required. Support PPAP, FAI, and other customer documentation requirements. Prepare technical evidence for customer approvals. Ensure customer-specific test methods are correctly implemented. I. Team Management & Development Lead and supervise laboratory personnel. Allocate daily laboratory activities. Monitor employee performance and discipline. Train laboratory personnel on testing methods, equipment, and safety. Develop technical competency of laboratory staff. Conduct skill-gap analysis and arrange technical training. EXPERIENCE REQUIRED Assistant Lab Manager 5–8 years of relevant experience in: Rubber formulation Rubber testing Laboratory operations Compound development/product qualification Lab Manager 8–15 years of relevant experience in: Rubber formulation and design Rubber testing laboratory Compound development Product qualification and validation Technical customer support/laboratory/team management Candidates with strong experience in aerospace rubber, sealing products, and critical applications will be preferred. 6. PREFERRED INDUSTRY EXPERIENCE Experience in one or more of the following industries will be preferred: Aerospace rubber components Aviation sealing systems Defense rubber products Navy applications Railway rubber components Oil & gas sealing products Nuclear applications 7. AEROSPACE & CRITICAL INDUSTRY RESPONSIBILITIES For aerospace and other critical applications, the lab manager shall: Ensure compliance with applicable AS9100 requirements. Maintain complete material and product traceability. Support NADCAP and customer audit requirements where applicable. Maintain strict control of laboratory records and technical documentation. Ensure controlled handling of critical materials and samples. Support FAI and product qualification requirements. Ensure validation and qualification testing is completed as per approved specifications. Maintain appropriate revision control of customer specifications and test methods.
